editorial.headline: Financial Leasing: Asset Finance With Bali’s PMA Door Open
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers finance-led leasing of client-selected assets, with national foreign ownership open to 100% and no Bali PMA moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Financial leasing is finance for the acquisition of assets in a client’s or customer’s name. The financier or lessor remains the legal owner, while the client or lessee carries the risk throughout the period of use—usually one that reflects the asset’s expected useful life—and receives the full benefit of using it. The model includes leasing arrangements with an option to purchase durable goods, such as vehicles. Its centre of gravity is therefore not simple rental, but the financing structure behind an asset’s use and eventual option rights.

The scope also accommodates conventional financing companies whose business covers the financing of goods and/or services: investment finance, working-capital finance, multipurpose finance, and other financing activities approved by the Financial Services Authority. Alongside those activities, such a company may conduct operating leases and/or fee-based activities, provided these do not conflict with financial-services law. The distinction matters: operating leasing without an option to purchase is not itself included in this activity’s defined scope, even though conventional financing companies in the group may undertake operating leases within the stated regulatory boundary.

Registration is open across every stated business scale, from Mikro and Kecil through Menengah and Besar. Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level; there is no lower foreign-equity cap to infer or work around from this entry.

For Bali, the position remains open rather than provisional. The province’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks Low and Medium-Low risk activities island-wide. This activity is not blocked by that rule: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk classification is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, placing it outside the moratorium’s blocked risk bands. A foreign investor can therefore register this activity in Bali today, with the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling intact and no Bali-specific ownership reduction or partnership condition stated in the record.
